name: contact-hub
purpose: The band under the Contact title band: the team lanes side by side (Sales and Support), each with its scope in one sentence and the action that reaches that team, over a row of self-serve channels. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'contact-hub', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `frame-box`, `card-grid`, `topic`, `button` and `status-indicator`. Lanes and channels share one frame, the channels in the rows under the lanes. A lane can carry a second button and a link to the system status page, so a reader can check for an incident before opening a ticket.
useWhen: On the Contact page, to route a reader to the team or channel that answers them.
avoidWhen: For a closing ask at the end of a page → use `closing-call-to-action`.
For a grid of product use cases → use `use-cases`.
related: topic` — each self-serve channel is a linked topic.
use-cases` — the sibling band of icon-led topics.
bestPractices: Give it as many lanes and channels as the page has: both rows balance themselves (`card-grid` `layout: 'balanced'`), so two channels split the row in halves, three in thirds, four into 2 × 2 and five into 3 + 2, with no empty cell.
Don't pad `channels` to three or drop one to make the row fit.
Keep each lane's description to one sentence that states what that team handles.
Set `target: '_blank'` on a channel or status link that leaves the site.
Lead each lane with its `action`; add a `secondaryAction` only for a second route to the same team (an outlined button after the first).
Give the band an `anchor` when a page links to it with a `#hash`.

props.name: anchor
props.doc: In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it.

props.name: lanes
props.doc: The team lanes side by side, in order; each is `{ icon, title, description, action?, secondaryAction?, statusLink? }` where `action` is the lane's leading button, `secondaryAction` an outlined button after it, and `statusLink` the system status link beside them.

props.name: channels
props.doc: The self-serve channels in the rows under the lanes, in order; each is `{ icon, title, description, href, target? }`, rendered as a linked topic.

examples.name: Default
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import ContactHub from '@aziontech/webkit/contact-hub'
</script>

<template>
  <ContactHub
    :lanes="[
      {
        icon: 'ai ai-briefcase',
        title: 'Sales',
        description:
          'Discuss your requirements, get custom pricing, or see the platform running on your own workload.',
        action: { label: 'Talk to sales', href: '/contact/sales' }
      },
      {
        icon: 'ai ai-headphones',
        title: 'Support',
        description:
          'Log in with your Azion account to open a ticket. Our engineers pick it up 24/7 on paid support plans.',
        action: {
          label: 'Log in to open a ticket',
          href: 'https://console.azion.com/login',
          trailing: true
        },
        statusLink: { label: 'System status', href: 'https://status.azion.com/', target: '_blank' }
      }
    ]"
    :channels="[
      {
        icon: 'ai ai-shield',
        title: 'Under a cyberattack?',
        description:
          'Get emergency mitigation for an attack in progress, even before you become a customer.',
        href: 'https://www.azion.com/en/lp/under-attack-mitigation/',
        target: '_blank'
      },
      {
        icon: 'ai ai-discord',
        title: 'Join the community',
        description: 'Ask developers and the Azion team on Discord. Open to everyone, on any plan.',
        href: 'https://discord.com/invite/pM8ANzztuB',
        target: '_blank'
      },
      {
        icon: 'ai ai-book',
        title: 'Read the docs',
        description: 'Guides, API reference, and troubleshooting for every Azion product.',
        href: 'https://www.azion.com/en/documentation/',
        target: '_blank'
      }
    ]"
  />
</template>
